question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
During winters, most of the trains are not running on time in North India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. are not running.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes a habitual/general fact about winters using the time expression "During winters", which signals a habitual action that recurs every winter.

• Rule — Simple Present Tense for habitual actions: When a sentence describes a general truth, habit, or repeated action (often signalled by words like always, usually, every day, during winters), the verb must be in the Simple Present Tense, not the Present Continuous Tense.

• The given segment "are not running" is in the Present Continuous Tense, which is used for actions happening right now or temporarily — not for a recurring seasonal habit. It should instead be "do not run".

◦ Corrected sentence: During winters, most of the trains do not run on time in North India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "During winters," is correct; it is a grammatically fine adverbial phrase of time that sets up the habitual context.

• Option 2: "on time in North India." is correct; it is a proper adverbial phrase of manner and place, with no grammatical fault.

• Option 4: "most of the trains" is correct; it is a grammatically sound subject phrase ("most of + plural noun" correctly takes a plural verb).

NOTE

• Time expressions such as "every day", "usually", "generally", "during winters/summers" typically demand the Simple Present Tense, even when the underlying idea feels ongoing.

• Common SSC trap: confusing an ongoing, temporary state (Present Continuous) with a recurring, general habit (Simple Present).

question:
The sentence below contains errors. Select the option with the correct use of tenses.
I will revised my course at least three times before my final examination.
option_1: I would revised my course at least three times before my final examination.
option_2: I will be revised my course at least three times since my final examination.
option_3: I will have revised my course at least three times before my final examination.
option_4: I must revised my course at least three times before my final examination.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. I will have revised my course at least three times before my final examination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The original sentence wrongly combines the modal "will" directly with the past-participle-looking form "revised"; a modal must be followed by the base form (V1), so "will revised" is ungrammatical.

• Rule — Future Perfect Tense: Used for an action that will be completed before a specified future time, often introduced by "before".

◦ Structure: Subject + will have + V3 (past participle) + Object + before + future time reference

• Applying the rule: since the revision will be completed before the final examination (a future point in time), the verb must take the Future Perfect form "will have revised".

◦ Corrected sentence: I will have revised my course at least three times before my final examination.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "would revised" wrongly pairs the modal "would" with a past-participle-like form instead of the base verb; also, "would" is used for past habitual or conditional contexts, not for a genuine future plan.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "will be revised" is a passive construction (which changes the meaning to "the course will be revised by someone"), and it wrongly uses "since" instead of "before", which does not fit the logical sequence of events.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "must revised" wrongly pairs the modal "must" with a past-participle-like form instead of the base verb "revise"; moreover, "must" expresses obligation, not future completion.

NOTE

• A modal verb (will, would, must, can, could, should, etc.) is always followed by the base form (V1) of the main verb, e.g. "will revise", never "will revised".

• The Future Perfect Tense is frequently tested with time markers such as "by the time", "before", "by next year".

question:
Select the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blank.
He comes here _________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. daily.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "comes" is in the Simple Present Tense, which is normally used to describe habitual or repeated actions.

• Rule — Adverbs of Frequency: Words like daily, always, usually, often, never, weekly indicate how often an action happens and naturally pair with the Simple Present Tense to describe a routine.

• Since the sentence describes a routine action ("He comes here"), the adverb of frequency "daily" fits perfectly and completes the sense of a regular habit.

◦ Completed sentence: He comes here daily.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "quickly" is an adverb of manner (describing how an action is performed), not of frequency, so it does not logically fit a blank asking about how often "he comes here".

• Option 2: "formerly" means "in the past" or "previously" and is generally used with the past tense, not with the Simple Present Tense verb "comes".

• Option 4: "lately" means "recently" and is normally used with the Present Perfect Tense (e.g. "He hasn't come here lately"), not with the Simple Present Tense.

NOTE

• Common adverbs of frequency: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never, daily, weekly, monthly.

• Common adverbs of time (often confused with frequency): lately, recently, formerly, previously, already, yet — these typically pair with Perfect tenses.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
That day we reached late for the competition and even though the competition went on smooth, I felt bad about Shivani losing it.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the competition went on smooth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb phrase "went on" is being modified — it needs a word that describes how the competition proceeded, i.e. it needs an adverb, not an adjective.

• Rule — Adjective vs Adverb: An adjective modifies a noun/pronoun, while an adverb modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. Adverbs of manner are usually formed by adding "-ly" to the adjective (e.g. smooth → smoothly).

• In the given segment, "smooth" (an adjective) is wrongly used to modify the verb "went on"; it must be replaced with the adverb "smoothly".

◦ Corrected segment: the competition went on smoothly

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "I felt bad" is correct; "bad" here correctly functions as an adjective complement after the linking verb "felt" (feel + adjective, not feel + adverb).

• Option 2: "losing it" is correct; the gerund "losing" is properly used as the object of the preposition "about".

• Option 4: "we reached late" is correct; "late" here is correctly used as an adverb of time modifying "reached" (note: "late" is one of the few words with the same form as adjective and adverb).

NOTE

• Common SSC trap words that are both adjective and adverb in the same spelling: late, hard, fast, high, early, straight (e.g. "he worked hard" — adverb).

• Other adjective-to-adverb pairs frequently tested: quick → quickly, smooth → smoothly, careful → carefully, quiet → quietly.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Hierarchy is key in ensuring normal functioning of our increasingly (1)_________ society. In the US, there is an enormous variety of industries, professional branches, specialisations, as well as a great (2)_______ of other domains of human activity or interests. So, competence here is valued and opinion influencers have an important role to play. In fact, leadership evolves as a necessity almost in any realm of human activity/ thinking, (3)______ where more people are involved.
Thus, it isn't hard (4)____ why even in academic institutions throughout the US and worldwide, students are given leadership essay assignments. Most students will take on leadership roles with various degrees of responsibility and impact in their lives, hence, becoming (5)______ with typical challenges, solutions, or skills required is essential.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. complex.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank describes the nature of "our... society" that necessitates hierarchy and leadership; the passage goes on to talk about "an enormous variety of industries, professional branches, specialisations", which is a description of complexity, not simplicity.

• Rule — Contextual vocabulary in cloze passages: The correct word must logically connect with the information that follows it in the passage (here, the idea of many varied industries and domains).

• Since the following sentence lists many industries, professional branches and specialisations, the society being described is becoming increasingly "complex" — this word logically links to the idea of variety and multiplicity that follows.

◦ Completed sentence: Hierarchy is key in ensuring normal functioning of our increasingly complex society.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "systematic" means organised in a planned, orderly way — this contradicts the idea of an "enormous variety" of domains, which suggests complexity rather than order.

• Option 3: "easy" does not fit logically; an "easy" society would not require hierarchy and leadership to function normally.

• Option 4: "fine" is vague and does not connect meaningfully with the idea of variety and specialisation described in the rest of the passage.

NOTE

• In cloze/fill-in-the-blank passages, always read the sentence(s) immediately after the blank — they usually provide the strongest contextual clue to the missing word.

• Words like complex, intricate, multifaceted, diverse are commonly used together in passages describing modern societies with many specialised fields.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. diversity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states there is "an enormous variety of industries, professional branches, specialisations, as well as a great (2)_______ of other domains of human activity or interests" — the word "variety" earlier in the sentence is a strong clue that the missing word must carry a similar meaning.

• Rule — Parallelism/Repetition of idea in a sentence: When a sentence already establishes an idea (here, "variety"), a later blank in the same sentence describing a similar concept should use a matching or synonymous term for consistency.

• "Diversity" means a range of different things/variety, and it correctly parallels "an enormous variety" mentioned earlier in the same sentence.

◦ Completed sentence: there is an enormous variety of industries... as well as a great diversity of other domains of human activity or interests.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "worry" does not fit; the sentence is not describing anxiety or concern about other domains.

• Option 2: "difficulty" does not logically connect with "a great ___ of other domains" in the sense of variety/multiplicity.

• Option 3: "uniformity" means sameness, which is the opposite of what the sentence is describing (variety and multiplicity of domains).

NOTE

• "Uniformity" and "diversity" are antonyms often tested together in vocabulary-based questions — do not confuse the two.

• Words like variety, diversity, range, and multiplicity are commonly interchangeable in passages describing many different types of something.

question:
Comprehension: In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Hierarchy is key in ensuring normal functioning of our increasingly (1)_________ society. In the US, there is an enormous variety of industries, professional branches, specialisations, as well as a great (2)_______ of other domains of human activity or interests. So, competence here is valued and opinion influencers have an important role to play. In fact, leadership evolves as a necessity almost in any realm of human activity/ thinking, (3)______ where more people are involved.
Thus, it isn't hard (4)____ why even in academic institutions throughout the US and worldwide, students are given leadership essay assignments. Most students will take on leadership roles with various degrees of responsibility and impact in their lives, hence, becoming (5)______ with typical challenges, solutions, or skills required is essential.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. especially.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "leadership evolves as a necessity almost in any realm of human activity/thinking, (3)______ where more people are involved." — the clause after the blank narrows down the general statement ("almost in any realm") to a specific condition ("where more people are involved").

• Rule — Use of "especially": "Especially" is used to single out or emphasise a particular case from a general statement, which is exactly the logical relationship here (the general "any realm" being narrowed to the specific case of "more people involved").

• Since the sentence first makes a general claim and then emphasises a particular condition under which the claim is even more true, "especially" is the correct connector.

◦ Completed sentence: leadership evolves as a necessity almost in any realm of human activity/thinking, especially where more people are involved.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "only" would wrongly restrict leadership's necessity to just this one case, contradicting the earlier phrase "almost in any realm".

• Option 3: "easily" is an adverb of manner and does not logically connect the general statement to the specific condition that follows.

• Option 4: "tactfully" means "in a diplomatic manner" and has no logical connection to the idea of emphasising a specific condition.

NOTE

• "Especially" and "particularly" are commonly interchangeable emphasising words frequently tested in SSC cloze passages.

• Distinguish "especially" (emphasising a specific case within a general statement) from "specially" (for a particular purpose) — a common SSC spelling/usage trap.

So, competence here is valued and opinion influencers have an important role to play. In fact, leadership evolves as a necessity almost in any realm of human activity/ thinking, (3)______ where more people are involved.
Thus, it isn't hard (4)____ why even in academic institutions throughout the US and worldwide, students are given leadership essay assignments. Most students will take on leadership roles with various degrees of responsibility and impact in their lives, hence, becoming (5)______ with typical challenges, solutions, or skills required is essential.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. accepting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Thus, it isn't hard (4)____ why even in academic institutions throughout the US and worldwide, students are given leadership essay assignments." — the passage is explaining that the reason behind this practice is easy to understand/accept, following logically from the earlier point about leadership's necessity.

• Rule — Contextual coherence: The chosen word must express the idea of comprehending or acknowledging the reason ("why...") given the evidence already discussed in the passage.

• "Accepting" fits the sense of readily acknowledging or understanding the given reason, continuing the passage's logical flow about the wide-reaching necessity of leadership.

◦ Completed sentence: Thus, it isn't hard accepting why... students are given leadership essay assignments.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "focusing" does not logically fit; the sentence is not about directing attention but about understanding/accepting a reason.

• Option 2: "rejecting" is the opposite of the intended sense; the passage is building a case for why leadership assignments make sense, not dismissing it.

• Option 3: "polishing" means refining or improving, which has no logical connection to explaining "why" something is done.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always check whether the word before/after the blank restricts the grammatical form needed (here, a word that can follow "hard" and precede "why").

• Commonly confused near-synonyms in SSC cloze passages: accept vs. except, accept vs. agree, accept vs. admit.

So, competence here is valued and opinion influencers have an important role to play. In fact, leadership evolves as a necessity almost in any realm of human activity/ thinking, (3)______ where more people are involved.
Thus, it isn't hard (4)____ why even in academic institutions throughout the US and worldwide, students are given leadership essay assignments. Most students will take on leadership roles with various degrees of responsibility and impact in their lives, hence, becoming (5)______ with typical challenges, solutions, or skills required is essential.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. familiar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...students will take on leadership roles... hence, becoming (5)______ with typical challenges, solutions, or skills required is essential." The phrase "___ with" is a strong clue to the required word.

• Rule — Fixed collocation "familiar with": The adjective "familiar" is conventionally followed by the preposition "with" to mean having good knowledge or understanding of something.

• Since the sentence talks about students gaining knowledge of "typical challenges, solutions, or skills", becoming "familiar with" them is the logical and grammatically correct choice.

◦ Completed sentence: becoming familiar with typical challenges, solutions, or skills required is essential.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "unusual" does not fit; students would not need to become "unusual with" challenges — this collocation does not exist in standard English.

• Option 3: "unequal" makes no logical sense with "with typical challenges" and is not a standard collocation.

• Option 4: "strange" is not conventionally followed by "with" in this sense, and would not logically describe a student gaining useful knowledge of challenges and skills.

NOTE

• Common fixed adjective + preposition collocations tested by SSC: familiar with, aware of, capable of, fond of, keen on, similar to.

• "Familiar with" (know well) should not be confused with "familiar to" (well-known to someone), a frequently tested SSC nuance.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Are today / a working day / or a / holiday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Are today.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "today", which is a singular noun (referring to a single day).

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement: A singular subject must take a singular verb form. For the verb "to be" in the Simple Present Tense, a singular subject takes "is", while a plural subject takes "are".

• Since "today" is singular, the verb must be "Is", not "Are".

◦ Corrected sentence: Is today a working day or a holiday?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "holiday" is grammatically correct; it is simply a noun completing the alternative question.

• Option 3: "a working day" is grammatically correct; it is a properly formed noun phrase.

• Option 4: "or a" is grammatically correct; it correctly introduces the second alternative in the either/or question structure.

NOTE

• Common SSC trap: singular time-reference nouns like today, yesterday, tomorrow, this week, this month always take a singular verb.

• Do not confuse this with plural subjects like "these days" or "the holidays", which require "are".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.
They appointed him as the manager, as he was due for an promotion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The rule for choosing between the articles "a" and "an" depends on the sound with which the following word begins, not merely its spelling.

• Rule — Use of "a" vs "an": Use "an" before a word beginning with a vowel sound, and use "a" before a word beginning with a consonant sound.

• The word "promotion" begins with the consonant sound /p/ (a "puh" sound), so it must be preceded by the article "a", not "an".

◦ Corrected sentence: he was due for a promotion.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "next" is incorrect; substituting "an" with "next" ("due for next promotion") is grammatically incomplete, as "next" alone cannot replace the article before a common noun in this construction.

• Option 2: "it's" is incorrect; "it's" (a contraction of "it is") makes no grammatical sense in place of an article before the noun "promotion".

• Option 3: "No substitution required" is incorrect because the original sentence does contain a genuine article error ("an promotion" is grammatically wrong).

NOTE

• The choice of "a"/"an" is based on pronunciation, not spelling — e.g. "an hour" (silent h, vowel sound) but "a university" (consonant "y" sound despite starting with a vowel letter).

• Commonly tested exceptions: a European, a one-rupee note, an MBA, an heir, a unit.

question:
Choose an appropriate word that can substitute the bracketed word and complete the sentence meaningfully.
What is the time (in) your watch?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. by.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The question asks for the correct preposition to use when referring to the time shown on a timekeeping device such as a watch or clock.

• Rule — Preposition "by" with time-telling devices: The preposition "by" is conventionally used to indicate the time as measured/shown by a clock or watch, e.g. "by my watch", "by the clock tower".

• Replacing "in" with "by" correctly conveys the intended meaning of asking what time the watch shows.

◦ Corrected sentence: What is the time by your watch?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "with" is incorrect; "with your watch" does not idiomatically express "as shown by the watch".

• Option 3: "into" is incorrect; "into" indicates movement or transformation and has no logical connection to reading time off a watch.

• Option 4: "on" is incorrect; "on your watch" is an idiom meaning "during the period one is responsible/on duty", which changes the intended meaning of the sentence.

NOTE

• Idiomatic prepositional usage: "by the watch/clock" (to state time), but "on someone's watch" (meaning "while someone is in charge/responsible") — a common SSC confusion.

• Other fixed time-related prepositional phrases: in time (not late), on time (punctually), in no time (very quickly).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
His grandfather was quite grumpy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Amiable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Grumpy" means easily irritated, bad-tempered, or sullen (चिड़चिड़ा / रूखे स्वभाव वाला).

◦ Example: The grumpy old man shouted at the children for playing near his gate.

• "Amiable" means friendly, good-natured, and pleasant in manner (मिलनसार / सौम्य स्वभाव वाला) — the direct opposite of being bad-tempered.

◦ Example: Despite his busy schedule, the manager remained amiable with all his staff.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Possible (संभव): Capable of happening or being done — unrelated to temperament.

• Option 2: Tenable (न्यायसंगत/बचाव योग्य): Able to be defended or maintained against attack or objection (e.g. a tenable argument) — unrelated to mood.

• Option 3: Edible (खाने योग्य): Fit to be eaten — unrelated to temperament.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "grumpy": irritable, cranky, sullen, testy, crotchety.

• Antonyms of "grumpy": amiable, cheerful, genial, affable, good-humoured.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
It's very cheap to display wealth by donning gaudy dresses.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sober.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Gaudy" means extravagantly bright, showy, or tastelessly ornamented (भड़कीला / चटकीला).

◦ Example: The gaudy decorations at the party looked more tacky than festive.

• "Sober" here means plain, restrained, and not showy in colour or style (सादा / संयमित) — the direct opposite of gaudy.

◦ Example: She preferred sober, well-tailored clothes over flashy outfits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Scanty (अपर्याप्त/कम): Insufficient or barely enough in amount — describes quantity, not showiness, so it is not a true antonym of "gaudy".

• Option 2: Ornate (अलंकृत): Elaborately decorated — this is actually close in meaning to "gaudy" (a near-synonym), not its opposite.

• Option 3: Cheap (सस्ता): Low in price or low in quality — gaudy items are often described as "cheap-looking", so this is closer to a synonym-associated word, not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "gaudy": flashy, garish, showy, loud, tawdry, ornate.

• Antonyms of "gaudy": sober, plain, subdued, tasteful, understated, elegant.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Apropriate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Appropriate" — meaning suitable or proper for a particular situation.

◦ Example: She wore appropriate clothing for the formal interview.

• Spelling key: AP + PRO + PRI + ATE. Note the double "p" after "A" (AP-PROPRIATE) — this is the letter most commonly dropped by mistake. The given option "Apropriate" incorrectly uses only a single "p".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Timorous" is spelt correctly — it means "showing fear or lack of confidence".

• Option 2: "Amalgamate" is spelt correctly — it means "to combine or merge to form one organisation or structure".

• Option 3: "Unintended" is spelt correctly — it means "not planned or meant".

NOTE

• Other commonly misspelt double-letter words tested by SSC: accommodate, embarrass, occurrence, committee, necessary, possession.

• Memory tip for "appropriate": think of it as "AP" + "PROPRIATE" — two P's, one right after "A" and one starting the next syllable.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
MOROSE
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Jovial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Morose" means sullen, gloomy, and ill-tempered (उदास / चिड़चिड़ा).

◦ Example: He has been morose ever since he lost his job.

• "Jovial" means cheerful, good-humoured, and full of high spirits (हंसमुख / प्रसन्नचित) — the direct opposite of being gloomy.

◦ Example: The jovial host kept all the guests laughing throughout the evening.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Practical (व्यावहारिक): Concerned with actual application rather than theory — unrelated to mood.

• Option 3: Dramatic (नाटकीय): Sudden and striking, or relating to drama — unrelated to being cheerful or gloomy.

• Option 4: Hurried (जल्दबाज़ी में): Done in haste — unrelated to temperament.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "morose": sullen, gloomy, glum, sulky, dour, melancholic.

• Antonyms of "morose": jovial, cheerful, jolly, genial, buoyant.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Despondency
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cheerfulness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Despondency" means a state of low spirits caused by loss of hope or courage (निराशा / हताशा).

◦ Example: A deep sense of despondency spread through the team after their defeat.

• "Cheerfulness" means a state of being noticeably happy and optimistic (प्रसन्नता / उल्लास) — the direct opposite of despondency.

◦ Example: Her cheerfulness brightened up the entire office.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Hopelessness (निराशा): This is a near-synonym of despondency, not its opposite.

• Option 2: Satisfaction (संतुष्टि): Means contentment; while positive, it is not the precise opposite of despondency in the way "cheerfulness" is.

• Option 4: Dejection (उदासी): This is also a near-synonym of despondency (a feeling of sadness), not an antonym.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "despondency": dejection, hopelessness, gloom, melancholy, desolation.

• Antonyms of "despondency": cheerfulness, optimism, hope, buoyancy, elation.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
The humble pupil sat on the floor with respect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Proud.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Humble" means having a modest or low estimate of one's own importance; not proud or arrogant (विनम्र / नम्र).

◦ Example: Despite his success, he remained humble and courteous to everyone.

• "Proud" means feeling deep pleasure or satisfaction from one's own achievements, often with a sense of self-importance; arrogant (घमंडी / अभिमानी) — the direct opposite of humble.

◦ Example: He became too proud after winning the competition and stopped listening to advice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Capitalist (पूंजीपति): A person who supports or practices capitalism, or a wealthy business owner — unrelated to humility.

• Option 2: Corrupt (भ्रष्ट): Dishonest or acting for illegitimate personal gain — unrelated in meaning to humility/pride.

• Option 3: Sturdy (मजबूत): Strongly and solidly built — unrelated to temperament or attitude.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "humble": modest, meek, unassuming, unpretentious, submissive.

• Antonyms of "humble": proud, arrogant, haughty, conceited, vain.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Sell like hot cakes
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Selling out quickly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Sell like hot cakes" means to be sold quickly and in large quantities, because the item is very popular or in high demand (तेज़ी से और बड़ी मात्रा में बिकना).

◦ Example: The new smartphone model sold like hot cakes within hours of its launch.

• The expression originates from the practice of selling freshly baked hot cakes at fairs, which used to be eaten and bought up almost as soon as they came off the griddle, due to their popularity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Extremely hot and humid (बहुत गर्म और उमस भरा): This is a literal misreading of the word "hot" in the idiom; the idiom is not about weather.

• Option 2: Not bothering about money (पैसों की परवाह न करना): This describes carelessness about money, unrelated to the idea of rapid, high-volume selling.

• Option 4: Become very famous (बहुत प्रसिद्ध हो जाना): While popularity may contribute to fast sales, the idiom specifically refers to the act of selling quickly, not to fame in general.

NOTE

• Other common SSC idioms about business/commerce: "To drive a hard bargain" (to negotiate toughly), "To foot the bill" (to pay for something), "To go for a song" (to sell very cheaply).

• Do not confuse "sell like hot cakes" (fast-selling due to demand) with "go for a song" (sold cheaply, opposite of high value).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
He hasn't _______ any attention to my miserable state.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. paid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence requires a verb that correctly collocates with the noun "attention" in the Present Perfect Tense (has/have + not + V3).

• Rule — Fixed collocation "pay attention": In English, the verb conventionally used with "attention" is "pay", forming the fixed expression "pay attention (to)", meaning to give one's focus or notice to something.

• Since the sentence is in the Present Perfect Tense ("hasn't ___ any attention"), the correct past participle form of "pay" — "paid" — must be used.

◦ Completed sentence: He hasn't paid any attention to my miserable state.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "made" is incorrect; "make attention" is not a standard English collocation.

• Option 2: "had" is incorrect; "have attention" is not the correct fixed expression for giving notice to something.

• Option 3: "gave" is incorrect grammatically (the Present Perfect Tense requires the past participle "given", not the simple past "gave"), and in any case "give attention" is not the standard idiomatic collocation — "pay attention" is.

NOTE

• Common fixed verb-noun collocations tested by SSC: pay attention, take care, make a decision, do damage, take a decision, give rise to.

• Remember: with the Present Perfect Tense (has/have), the past participle (V3) form of the verb must always be used, e.g. "paid" (not "pay" or "gave").

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.
She developing a remarkable resistance to cold and altitude.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. developed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "developing" is a bare present participle (a non-finite verb form) used here without any helping/auxiliary verb, so the sentence has no finite main verb and is grammatically incomplete.

• Rule — Every sentence needs a finite verb: A present participle (V-ing) cannot function alone as the main verb of a sentence; it must either be preceded by a suitable auxiliary (is/was/has been, etc.) or replaced by a finite verb form.

• The simplest and most direct correction is to replace the incomplete participle with the finite Simple Past Tense form "developed", which completes the sentence with a single, definite main verb.

◦ Corrected sentence: She developed a remarkable resistance to cold and altitude.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "has develop" is incorrect because the Present Perfect Tense requires the past participle form after "has" — it should be "has developed", not "has develop".

• Option 3: "No substitution required" is incorrect because the original sentence, as it stands with the bare participle "developing" and no auxiliary verb, is grammatically incomplete.

• Option 4: "has been developing" is grammatically well-formed (Present Perfect Continuous), but it is not the intended minimal correction here; the sentence is meant to describe a single, definite action, correctly and simply expressed with the Simple Past "developed".

NOTE

• A verb ending in "-ing" used without any auxiliary verb ("is/was/has been/were") can never stand alone as the finite verb of a sentence — this is one of the most common SSC error-spotting/correction traps.

• Compare tenses: Simple Past ("developed") for a completed action; Present Perfect Continuous ("has been developing") for an action that began in the past and is still continuing.

question: Which of the following idioms means 'going to sleep'?
option_1: Keep an ear to the ground
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Hit the sack.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Hit the sack" means to go to bed; to go to sleep (सोने जाना / बिस्तर पर जाना).

◦ Example: It's already midnight — I think I'll hit the sack now.

• The expression is believed to come from the old practice of stuffing a cloth sack with straw to use as a mattress; "hitting" (lying down on) the sack meant going to bed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Keep an ear to the ground" (स्थिति पर नज़र रखना): To stay alert and well-informed about developments or rumours.

• Option 2: "Run around in circles" (बिना किसी परिणाम के प्रयास करना): To make a great deal of effort without achieving anything useful.

• Option 3: "Break new grounds" (नई शुरुआत करना): To make an innovative advance or do something that has not been done before.

NOTE

• Other common SSC idioms meaning "to sleep": "Turn in", "Catch some Z's", "Snooze off".

• Do not confuse "hit the sack" (go to sleep) with "hit the road" (to leave/start a journey) or "hit the books" (to study hard).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Agressive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Aggressive" — meaning ready or likely to attack or confront; behaving in a forceful, hostile manner.

◦ Example: The dog became aggressive when strangers approached the gate.

• Spelling key: AG + GRESS + IVE. Note the double "g" (AG-GRESSIVE) — this is the letter most commonly dropped by mistake. The given option "Agressive" incorrectly uses only a single "g".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Creator" is spelt correctly — it means "a person or thing that creates something".

• Option 2: "Skewed" is spelt correctly — it means "distorted or biased in a particular direction".

• Option 4: "Apparent" is spelt correctly — it means "clearly visible or understood; obvious".

NOTE

• Other commonly misspelt double-letter words tested by SSC: accommodate, embarrass, occurrence, committee, necessary, possession, appropriate.

• Memory tip for "aggressive": it comes from Latin "aggredi" (to attack), retaining the double "g" from "ad- + gradi".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.
The setting sun turned the _________(calm) ocean into a sea of gold.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. placid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed word "calm" means free from disturbance; still and peaceful (शांत).

◦ Example: The lake was calm and undisturbed in the early morning.

• "Placid" means calm and peaceful, without much disturbance or movement, especially describing a stretch of water (शांत / स्थिर) — a close synonym of "calm".

◦ Example: The boat glided smoothly across the placid lake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Volatile (अस्थिर/उग्र): Liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse — this is closer to an antonym of "calm", not a synonym.

• Option 3: Furtive (चोरी-छिपे): Attempting to avoid notice or attention, typically because of guilt or a wish to conceal something — unrelated to calmness.

• Option 4: Scattered (बिखरा हुआ): Spread out in different directions or over a wide area — unrelated to calmness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "calm": placid, serene, tranquil, still, peaceful.

• Antonyms of "calm": volatile, turbulent, agitated, stormy, choppy.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
He is just jealous that he didn't get picked for the job.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. envious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Jealous" means feeling or showing envy of someone or their achievements/advantages (ईर्ष्यालु).

◦ Example: She felt jealous when her friend got the promotion she had wanted.

• "Envious" means feeling discontented or resentful longing aroused by someone else's possessions, qualities, or luck (ईर्ष्यालु) — a direct synonym of "jealous".

◦ Example: He was envious of his colleague's quick success at the company.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Spiteful (द्वेषपूर्ण): Showing malice or a desire to hurt, annoy, or offend someone — this carries a sense of active malice, which goes beyond the meaning of simple jealousy.

• Option 3: Greedy (लालची): Having an excessive desire for more of something, especially wealth or food — describes acquisitiveness, not envy of another's success.

• Option 4: Suspicious (शंकालु): Having or showing a cautious distrust of someone or something — describes distrust, not envy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "jealous": envious, covetous, resentful, green-eyed.

• Antonyms of "jealous": content, satisfied, generous, unenvious.
